findings.mechanism: Its passive perfect form takes the following imperative as quoted content, so the order foregrounds what the group is told to do.
findings.reader_payoff: The instruction confronts the addressees before the scene names their reply.
findings.containment: The passive form suppresses the immediate human agent; it does not make the command source neutral.

epistemic.reason: The passive morphology and attachment to the imperative are explicit; cited formula parallels are excluded.

findings.title: The passive command still has an addressee

findings.mechanism: Although the speaker is left unstated, li-hum supplies the people to whom the words are directed; their later reply fills that addressee slot.
findings.reader_payoff: The command is concrete and directed, not an abstract maxim.
findings.containment: The phrase identifies the addressees without supplying a new human speaker.

epistemic.reason: The preposition governs the following plural pronoun as the recipient complement.

findings.mechanism: The plural pronoun after the passive report returns as the attached object of yadʿūhum; within the focus ayah, one group is carried from recipient to target.

findings.containment: Only the focus-internal pronoun chain is retained; the identity of the group in 31:20 is not imported.

epistemic.reason: The same plural reference is grammatically recoverable within the focus; prior-ayah identification is excluded.

findings.title: The command’s action has consequences

findings.mechanism: Both clauses use the following action, while the ending attaches an adverse destination to the group’s chosen course; the command itself remains a demand to follow revelation.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader senses that a following claim carries consequences without making the command verb mean punishment.
findings.containment: The liability facet colors the focus-wide action through its ending; it does not make following revelation itself culpable.

epistemic.reason: The candidate explicitly narrows consequence pressure to the action’s later destination; the ordinary following sense is retained.
